description: Resolving an asserted subject against the signed registry. Anything not proven is the named state subject_unproven{reason}.

cases.title: a registered, active agent asserted by its principal resolves
asserted by an authorised submitter (the gateway tenant) resolves
an unregistered subject is subject_unproven{not_registered}
an unreadable registry is subject_unproven{registry_unreadable}
a registration whose envelope did not verify
a submitter that is neither the principal nor authorised
a subject that is its own principal
a suspended subject
a retired subject (replaced agent)
the registry says merchant, the Grant says agent
two records for one ADI are ambiguous, not "the newest wins"
a malformed record (no responsible seat)
a single v2 registration, active, resolves
a suspension is a new version: the head decides, the subject is suspended
a reactivation is another new version: the subject resolves again
a retirement is a new version: retired
retired is terminal: a later version that reactivates is refused
a retired ADI cannot be registered again: a second version 1 is a fork
a version gap refuses the lineage
a wrong prior hash refuses the lineage
one version that does not verify refuses the whole lineage (fail closed)
the principal may not change across versions: a new principal is a new subject
the type may not change across versions
a v1 record and a v2 lineage for one ADI are refused as mixed
a new version may change the submitters: the new gateway resolves
a v2 registration whose principal is a sub-ADI of the subject is refused
a version 1 that carries a prior hash is malformed
time may not go backwards across versions
an assertion without an assertedBy is malformed
an expected type that is not a subject type is malformed
a registration signed by a key of the principal book verifies
a registration signed by the subject own key is registration_signed_by_subject
a registration signed by a key that is not on a page of the principal book is signer_not_principal
a Grant tag on a registration is refused
an envelope over another registration hash is registration_hash_mismatch
a certen-subjects account whose authority set includes a subject book is refused
a certen-subjects account whose authority set lacks the principal book is principal_not_authority
both roles present: the principal book and the subject own book each reach their threshold
the subject acceptance is missing: signatures of the principal alone are refused
a key of the principal that is also listed on a subject page cannot be the acceptance (the principal signs with its second key, the first key is offered as the acceptance)
an acceptance signed by a stranger key that is on no page of the subject book
an acceptance on a page of a book that is not a book of the subject
an acceptance replayed from another registration (made for version 2, presented on version 1) does not verify
a subject page of threshold 2 with one acceptance signature
an acceptance signature with a flipped byte
an acceptance with an unsupported algorithm
the principal role is checked first: a stranger key on the principal page is signer_not_principal even with a good acceptance
the subject cannot register itself: an envelope that holds only the acceptance has no principal role
acceptance is not authority: a subject key placed on a page of the principal book is still registration_signed_by_subject
a lineage whose versions each carry both roles resolves; each version is read against the snapshot as of its own entry, so a later rotation of the subject key does not invalidate version 1
a lineage in which version 2 lacks the acceptance is refused as a whole (fail closed)
a squatter: a principal that registers another ADI as its subject without the subject acceptance never resolves
a registration with the subject acceptance written before it resolves; the evidence is chain enforced, no key page is read
no acceptance account at all: the subject never consented
an acceptance written after the registration does not cover it: at the registration time the subject had not consented
the subject revoked its acceptance later: the registration no longer resolves
an acceptance that names another principal is not an acceptance of this one
an acceptance account whose authority set also holds another book is not the subject own account
an acceptance account whose authority changed after creation is refused by name
an acceptance account that is not a book of the subject is refused
an acceptance entry that is not the canonical text refuses the read of the account
a suspension needs no acceptance: the principal alone decreases, even after the subject revoked its acceptance
a retirement needs no acceptance either
a reactivation is an increase and needs the acceptance in force at its time: revoked, so refused
a reactivation with a fresh acceptance in force resolves
a change of submitters while active is not an increase and needs no new acceptance
a registration by ANOTHER ADI is invisible to this Grant: only the registry of the grantor is read
the grantor own registration resolves while another ADI also registered the same subject in its own registry
a registration in the grantor registry whose principal is another ADI is refused
a registry account whose authority changed after creation is refused by name
a registry account that holds a subject book is refused
a registry account owned by a book that is not the grantor book of this Grant is refused
block indexes of two accounts are unrelated: the registration is at a LOWER index but a later time than the acceptance, and it resolves
and the same with the indexes the other way round: only the times are compared
an accept and a revoke in the same second: the later position wins, so the consent is revoked
a revoke and an accept in the same second: the later position wins, so the consent stands
the acceptance in the same second as the registration counts: ties across accounts resolve as at or before
accept, revoke, accept with identical bytes are three entries: the registration sees the first accept, the head the last
an acceptance entry that was not delivered makes the acceptance account unreadable
an acceptance entry for which the node gave no block makes the acceptance account unreadable, never an invented time
a registration entry that was not delivered makes the registry unreadable
a reactivation written BEFORE the fresh acceptance stays refused: the acceptance that comes later does not repair version 3
a later version written after the fresh acceptance does not repair it either: every version is judged at its own entry time
a registry entry that carries no chain time makes the registry unreadable by name, never an invented time
an acceptance entry that carries no chain time makes the acceptance account unreadable by name
an acceptance entry that names another subject refuses the read of the account
a reactivation written BEFORE the fresh acceptance is pending, not burned: once the acceptance is written it is in force, from the acceptance time
no retroactive authority: the same registry judged at a time after the revocation and before the acceptance does not resolve the subject
at exactly the acceptance time the increase is in force (at or before)
a later version written after the acceptance resolves too: the reactivation of version 3 is no longer burned
a registration of version 1 written before the subject accepted resolves from the acceptance time
the same registration judged before the acceptance was written is subject_acceptance_missing
a registration whose acceptance came first is in force from its own entry time
a retirement written while a reactivation still waits for its acceptance ends the subject: the waiting increase never takes effect
a suspension written while a reactivation waits is the status in force, whatever the acceptance does later
the acceptance in the same second as the waiting version counts as at or before
an entry written after the evaluation time does not exist yet: a registry judged before its first entry has no registration
a change of submitters while active keeps the activation time of the version that registered
an evaluation time that is not a non-negative safe integer is refused as malformed input
an activation mode that is not named is refused as malformed input
the acceptance revoked after the activation ends the resolution, as before
a reactivation whose acceptance is still revoked is pending and does not resolve: the verdict of sr-64, with the rule stated correctly
a reactivation with the fresh acceptance already in force is in force from its own entry time: the verdict of sr-65, with the rule stated correctly
a certen.subject/v1 record in the registry account refuses the read of the account: the online reader reads certen.subject/v2 only (DAX3A-R3-6)
an acceptance account owned by a book under a sub-ADI of the subject is refused: the owner must be a key book in the authority set of the subject ADI itself (DAX3A-R3-3)
a grantor with no certen-subjects account (the node answers not found, which is an answer): not_registered (DAX3B-F10)
a registry account that could not be read (a transport failure, never an answer): registry_unreadable, which a gateway answers as a retryable 503 (DAX3B-F10)
a registration that was active and is now suspended, with no acceptance account at all, is subject_suspended: the head answers before any acceptance is read (GR-56, DAXCORE2-F4)
a registration that was active and is now retired, with no acceptance account at all, is subject_retired
a suspended head with an acceptance account that is not the subject own account is still subject_suspended: that account is not read for a decrease
a retired head with an acceptance account whose authority changed is still subject_retired
a suspended head whose acceptance was revoked is subject_suspended (the principal decided; the revocation is not consulted)
the control: an ACTIVE head with no acceptance account is still subject_acceptance_missing (only a decrease is answered first)
